newsitem.title: USA: Fla. robberies financed weekly court payments-paper.
newsitem.headline: Fla. robberies financed weekly court payments-paper.

text.p: A Florida man was charged in a series of Monday bank robberies that police said enabled him to make court-ordered restitution payments due the next day.
Tipsters led police to Donald Lewis Dingerson, who was charged Friday with 11 counts of bank robbery, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel reported Saturday.
Police, Broward County Sheriff's deputies and the FBI had been looking for him since the series of bank robberies began April 14 in the Fort Lauderdale area.

"This guy was hitting every week and then he didn't hit for about 10 days and we were wondering what the heck. We found out he was in jail from May 7 to May 11 for violation of probation," sheriff's Detective Jim Young told the Sun-Sentinel. "Two days after he was released he robbed a bank again."

Young said police were puzzled as to why most of the robberies occurred on Mondays. Dingerson confessed to the robberies, explaining that he was scheduled to meet his parole officer on Tuesdays to make restitution payments to his victims in previous criminal cases, the newspaper said.

Dingerson's criminal record included convictions for grand theft, cocaine possession and passing bad checks. When police caught up with him Friday, he was already in jail on charges of violating his probation by failing to make a restitution payment.
